title: Ethiopian Spiced Grilled Fish
community: Ethiopian lakeside restaurants — the charcoal-grilled whole fish
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Grilled Spiced Fish — whole fish scored and marinated in berbere, garlic, and lemon, grilled over charcoal until the berbere skin caramelises. The lakeside tradition — whole fish over charcoal, the smoke and berbere combining into one of Ethiopia's finest flavour experiences.
longDesc: Grilled whole fish is the cooking style of Ethiopia's lakeside restaurants — the freshly caught fish, scored deeply, rubbed with berbere inside and out, grilled over charcoal. The berbere caramelises on the skin as the smoke penetrates through the score marks. Eaten with injera and fresh salad at a table by the water.
ingredients: 2 whole fish (500g each) — tilapia, Nile perch, or catfish, cleaned and scaled
// Inside the cavity: sliced onion, garlic, jalapeño, coriander
steps: Score fish deeply — 3—4 cuts per side, 1cm deep.
Mix marinade. Rub inside and into score marks. Fill cavity with onion, garlic, jalapeño.
Grill over medium charcoal: 8—10 minutes per side.
The berbere skin should be caramelised and slightly charred.
chefTips: Score deeply — berbere must reach the flesh.
Medium charcoal — berbere burns at high heat.
Stuffing the cavity with aromatics perfumes the fish from within.
cookingScience: Scoring fish creates channels through the skin — the skin is the primary barrier to heat and flavour transfer in whole-fish cookery. Deep scoring dramatically accelerates both heat penetration (reducing cooking time) and marinade penetration (enhancing flavour).
sustainabilityTips: Whole fish from Ethiopian lakes — the most complete use of the catch.
culturalNote: Grilled spiced fish at a lakeside restaurant is one of Ethiopia's great dining experiences — the view of Lake Tana or Lake Hawassa, the smell of charcoal and berbere, the whole fish arriving fragrant and crispy. It is a food memory that Ethiopian travelers carry for decades.
